questions.question: Dividing a population into homogeneous groups before sample selection is called:
questions.explanation: Stratification divides the population into internally homogeneous strata, improving precision within each group.

questions.question: Probability proportional to size (PPS) sampling is used mainly to:
options: Give larger units a higher selection chance
questions.explanation: PPS assigns higher selection probabilities to larger units so estimates reflect their contribution.

questions.question: The design effect compares the efficiency of a complex sample against:
questions.explanation: The design effect measures variance inflation relative to a simple random sample of the same size.

questions.question: A pilot test of a questionnaire is primarily used to:
options: Detect ambiguous wording before the main round
questions.explanation: Pilot testing surfaces ambiguous or faulty question wording before the main survey round.

questions.question: A fixed reference period such as a 30-day recall window is used to:
questions.explanation: Fixed, short recall windows reduce respondent recall error in household surveys.

questions.question: Which of the following is a source of non-sampling error?
questions.explanation: Non-sampling errors arise from coverage mistakes, respondent errors and processing mistakes.

questions.question: A range check confirms that:
options: Numeric values fall between plausible limits
questions.explanation: Range checks confirm numeric values fall between plausible minimum and maximum limits.

questions.question: A consistency check compares:
options: Related fields such as age and date of birth
questions.explanation: Consistency checks compare related fields, such as age against date of birth.

questions.question: Skip logic validation ensures that:
options: Unanswered questions follow the correct filter pattern
questions.explanation: Skip logic validation ensures unanswered questions follow the correct questionnaire filter pattern.

questions.question: The standard error measures:
options: The variability of an estimate across repeated samples
questions.explanation: The standard error measures how much an estimate would vary across repeated samples.

questions.question: A 95% confidence interval means that:
options: 95% of the data lie inside the interval
The procedure captures the true value in 95% of repeated samples
questions.explanation: A confidence interval refers to the long-run coverage of the estimation procedure, not the data.

questions.question: Weighting adjustments primarily correct for:
questions.explanation: Weights correct for unequal selection probabilities and compensate for non-response.

questions.question: Which chart best shows the change of an indicator over time?
questions.explanation: Line charts are the standard choice for trends over time.

questions.question: A histogram is used to display:
options: The distribution of a numeric variable
questions.explanation: Histograms show the empirical distribution of a numeric variable.

questions.question: Data storytelling in government reports mainly aims to:
options: Make findings understandable to non-technical readers
questions.explanation: Data storytelling makes analytical findings accessible to non-technical decision makers.

questions.question: In R or Python, a data frame is:
options: A table of rows and columns
questions.explanation: A data frame is a rectangular table of rows (observations) and columns (variables).

questions.question: Which task is best handled by a scripting language such as R?
questions.explanation: Scripts make cleaning and analysis reproducible end-to-end from raw data.

questions.question: A reproducible analysis pipeline mainly requires:
options: Scripts that run end-to-end from raw data
questions.explanation: Reproducibility requires scripted, end-to-end processing from raw data to results.

sections.label: Introduction to Sampling
sections.text: The National Sample Survey relies on scientifically designed sampling frames to produce representative estimates. A sampling frame is the complete list of sampling units from which the sample is drawn. Stratification divides the population into homogeneous groups called strata before selection. Probability proportional to size sampling assigns higher selection probability to larger units. Systematic sampling selects every kth unit from the list after a random start. Cluster sampling surveys entire groups of nearby households to reduce field travel cost. Multistage sampling combines selection of villages first and households second. Sample size depends on the precision target and the population variance. Weighting adjustments correct for unequal selection probabilities and non-response. The design effect measures the loss of efficiency due to clustering compared to simple random sampling. Non-sampling errors arise from coverage mistakes, respondent errors and processing mistakes. Pilot testing of the questionnaire detects ambiguous wording before the main survey round. Reference period recall errors are reduced by using a fixed thirty day window.

sections.label: Field Operations
sections.text: Field investigators must verify the enumeration area boundaries before listing households. Supervisors spot check ten percent of completed schedules for quality control. Spot checks re-interview a small subset of households to detect fabrication of responses. Replacement households are selected only after three genuine contact attempts fail. The response rate is the ratio of completed interviews to eligible households contacted.

sections.label: Data Processing
sections.text: Data editing rules flag out-of-range values and skip pattern violations. Imputation fills missing values using nearest neighbour donor methods. Outliers are reviewed against source documents before any correction is applied. The validation plan documents every check applied to each variable.

sections.label: Validation Concepts
sections.text: Data validation confirms that each recorded value conforms to its expected format and range. Range checks confirm numeric values fall between plausible minimum and maximum limits. Consistency checks compare related fields such as age and date of birth. Skip logic validation ensures unanswered questions follow the correct filter pattern. Duplicate detection identifies records sharing identical identifiers across datasets. Checksum verification confirms that transmitted files arrive without corruption. The golden source principle states that one designated system holds the authoritative copy.

sections.label: Quality Management
sections.text: A data quality dashboard tracks timeliness, completeness and accuracy indicators. Root cause analysis traces recurring validation failures back to their source process. Correction logs preserve the original value alongside every modified entry. Reconciliation compares aggregated totals against independent administrative records. A data steward is the named officer accountable for the quality of a dataset. Escalation rules define when unresolved validation errors must be reported upward.
